briefdescription.para: An interval map for closed integer ranges. The mapped values are unused.

detaileddescription.para: This method does /not/ support setting a bit that has already been set, for efficiency reasons. If possible, restructure your code to not set the same bit multiple times, or use test_and_set.

briefdescription.para: Set the bits set in Other.

detaileddescription.para: This method does /not/ support setting already-set bits, see set for the rationale. For a safe set union operation, use operator|=.

Return an iterator pointing to the first set bit AT, OR AFTER, Index.

detaileddescription.para: If no such set bit exists, return end(). This is like std::lower_bound. This has worst-case logarithmic performance (roughly O(log(gaps between contiguous ranges))).

briefdescription.para: Return a range iterator which iterates over all of the set bits in the half-open range [Start, End).

briefdescription.para: Given the set of overlaps between this and some other bitvector, and an interval [Start, Stop] from that bitvector, determine the portions of the interval which do not overlap with this.
A bitvector that, under the hood, relies on an IntervalMap to coalesce elements into intervals.

detaileddescription.para: Good for representing sets which predominantly contain contiguous ranges. Bad for representing sets with lots of gaps between elements.
Compared to SparseBitVector, CoalescingBitVector offers more predictable performance for non-sequential find() operations.

parameterdescription.para: - The type of the index into the bitvector.
